subject: Post-call recap: Acme Corp - TCO & token economics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acmecorp.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme Corp - TCO & token economics

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture next steps.

Key pain points you shared:
- Token run-rate sensitivity: current pilot shows heavy per-token spend and unpredictable monthly bills during spikes.
- Latency requirements: sub-200ms for 95th pct on short chat flows is critical for product launch.
- Budget constraint: finance has set a 2026 inference ops budget target of ~$50k/year for this initial phase.
- Data controls: need audit logs and key management for PII-sensitive prompts.

Goals you want to hit:
- Move from prototype to pilot with a predictable TCO that fits the $50k/yr budget.
- Keep latency SLOs while reducing per-token cost.
- Validate feature parity for safety/traceability.

Cost / TCO highlights we discussed:
- Token economics: at your observed mix (avg request 120 tokens, 60k requests/day) we estimate ~216M tokens/month. Using our hosted model profile, baseline cost is roughly $X/month. (See attached spreadsheet for line-item math.)
- Batching & caching levers: enabling prefix KV caching for repeated prompts and 40–80ms batching windows on dedicated pools can reduce token spend by ~25–40% for your workload shape.
- Quantization / model variant: switching to our 8-bit variant for non-critical paths reduces GPU unit cost and can cut inference spend another 15–25% with minimal quality degradation in your tests.
- Routing policy: route dev/training traffic to lower-cost pools and production to higher-SLA pools to avoid unnecessary spend.

Preliminary ROI framing:
- With caching + batching + quantized model profile we expect a 35–55% reduction in monthly inference spend compared to current baseline while preserving 95th pct latency targets. That puts you within the stated budget range depending on final QPS growth.

Attachments I’m sharing:
- Acme-TCO-v1.xlsx: input-driven model (rows: qps, avg tokens, cache-hit rate, pricing per model variant).
- redwood-token-econ.pdf: short explainer on batching, KV caching, and quantization levers.
- mutual-action-plan.docx: suggested milestones and owners.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share the TCO workbook (attached) with a few scenarios — please confirm which scenario aligns best with Finance (conservative / target / stretch).
2) Schedule a 45-min architecture deep-dive next week to validate latency and caching feasibility (I’ll include Rafael from our infra team).
3) If the scenario looks good, we’ll prepare a 30-day pilot proposal with Dedicated burst capacity and an entry-level commitment to hit your SLA.

Can you confirm which TCO scenario Finance prefers and your availability for a deep-dive next Tue/Wed?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: Acme-TCO-v1.xlsx, redwood-token-econ.pdf, mutual-action-plan.docx

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme Corp - TCO & token economics

Thanks Marissa — very helpful summary.

Couple quick clarifications from our side:
- The 60k requests/day figure I quoted is average; peak days can be 2–3x that. Finance wants the conservative scenario (assume 2x peak for budgeting).
- Our $50k/yr cap is for inference-only spend for the pilot; we can be flexible on infra support and integration budget.

I’m available Tue 4/20 after 10am PT for the deep-dive. Please loop in Rafael and anyone who can speak to caching/latency trade-offs.

Also, can you highlight in the workbook a conservative scenario that includes a 50% cache hit rate vs a 20% hit rate? That will help us justify the pilot internally.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Director of Product, Acme Corp
sanjay@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmecorp.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme Corp - TCO & token economics (Updated workbook)

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks — I updated the workbook and attached 3 scenarios: conservative (2x peak, 20% cache hit), target (1.5x peak, 35% cache hit), and stretch (1x avg, 50% cache hit). See the 'Summary' tab for side-by-side monthly and annual totals.

Notes on assumptions:
- We modeled batching impact as a function of request size distribution; for your conversational mix, a 40ms batching window yields ~18% token-level cost savings and ~5–15ms added p95 latency on our Dedicated pools.
- KV/prefix caching assumptions: 20–50% hit rates were modeled depending on prompt repetitiveness; we included sensitivity rows.
- Quantized variant is modeled as 30% cheaper GPU utilization with a 3–5% quality metric delta (based on our eval set).

Next steps:
- I’ll schedule Tue 4/20 10:30am PT for a 45-min architecture deep-dive (invite to follow). Rafael, Vivek — can you both join to cover runtime and pricing options?
- Sanjay / Priya: if you want, we can lock in a small Dedicated pilot (30 days) with a capped commitment and a mutual-action plan to test caching and batching in production traffic.

If that works I’ll send the calendar invite and a short agenda.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme TCO — prep for Tue deep-dive

Marissa / Vivek —

Quick internal note ahead of the 4/20 deep-dive:
- I reviewed the workbook; the batching assumptions look reasonable but we should validate request size distribution with Acme before committing to the 40ms window. Edge case: very short 1–3 token requests will widen tail latency if batched too aggressively.
- For commercial framing: recommend offering a 3-week pilot with a capped spend of $12k and a performance SLA (p95 latency target) tied to a one-time credit if missed. This aligns with their $50k/yr cap while giving us runway to prove savings.
- I’ll prepare a 1-slide cost/benefit to include in the invite. Vivek — please pull any recent quantization benchmarks you can share.

Will be on the Tue call.

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
